messages.author: 53dbab5845ace6b6
messages.subject: Re: Error: Object 'stms' not found
parts:
Hmm... the R version should not matter (I have 4.1.0 and still no errors).
Something else must be the problem, perhaps another installed package that, when loaded, interferes with the normal commands from package QCA.

I see you have a lot of packages attached (no less than 23). This is not a particularly good idea, because functions with the same names can be found in different packages and, depending which package you've loaded last, it will have precedence.

I'd say the script worked on R version 4.0.4 simply because you did not have the other packages installed and loaded.

Best,
Adrian

If you want to get to the ground of this, Joanne, you could use your old setup and see whether the commands work when adding the package to the command: QCA::pof(conds, dummy.data$outcome). Am 02.06.2021 um 11:24 schrieb Adrian Dușa:
Hmm... the R version should not matter (I have 4.1.0 and still no errors).
Something else must be the problem, perhaps another installed package that, when loaded, interferes with the normal commands from package QCA.

I see you have a lot of packages attached (no less than 23). This is not a particularly good idea, because functions with the same names can be found in different packages and, depending which package you've loaded last, it will have precedence.

I'd say the script worked on R version 4.0.4 simply because you did not have the other packages installed and loaded.

Best,
Adrian

To anyone interested, I've been exchanging a couple of more emails with Joanne.
The error seems to be related to the computer's locale, in her case Chinese Traditional, which uses a multi-byte character encoding.

After a couple of trials and errors, I seem to have found a workaround published in the latest development version of package admisc on GitHub.
But since this type of error is marginally affecting only a very small number of users, I will wait for a while until publishing a new official version on CRAN.

Best wishes, I hope this helps,
Adrian
